## Introduction and Research Question

Gary Higgins, head coach of NC State's Women's Soccer Team, is coming off a successful season in which the team compiled a record of 11 wins, 5 losses, and 2 draws. This marks a significant improvement from the previous season's record of 5 wins, 9 losses, and 4 draws. Looking ahead, Higgins is interested in identifying areas where the team can continue to improve.

In Higgins's opinion, one of the most important statistics in soccer is turnover differential. He has asked the great up-and-coming statistician Ty Garrett to conduct a two-sample t-test comparing the mean turnover differential of graduating seniors with that of underclassmen to determine whether there is statistically significant evidence that seniors have a higher mean turnover differential.

If seniors demonstrate a significantly higher mean turnover differential, the team could potentially lose valuable production through graduation. If the test does not find sufficient evidence of a difference, we cannot conclude the team will improve, but the results may suggest that graduating seniors do not have a statistically significant advantage in this particular statistic. To investigate this question, Ty Garrett manually collected data during the team's first four home games of the season. This started off as something he did for fun because he was extremely unemployed with an insignificant amount of school work to do at the time. However, he is glad that he can finally turn this data into something useful.

A link to the full data set can found here:

https://1drv.ms/x/c/febd9e0d5722e8e5/IQD4EwFD6w0uSIxgRh7-ydFfAR8-7eoGOJK2lqX\_-5bppo4?e=U9JuC3

For this assignment, the analysis will include only graduating seniors who started and their likely underclassmen backups. Including all underclassmen could introduce potential differences into the analysis, as forwards naturally incur more turnovers while defenders generally have more opportunities to record takeaways.
